# Architecture

Diagnostic completion is a separate owner-delegation boundary. It ensures the
persisted Placement and reads durable planning-state, without submitting a
plan. The explicit diagnostic alternative on the existing planning facade uses
the plan identity as idempotency key and owner-derived goal/context. Teacher
stores no new learner or workflow table. On reload, the same completion call
projects the existing Placement/job; Student confirms any active path claim.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant UI
    participant Teacher
    participant Planner
    participant Student
    UI->>Teacher: Complete {plan_id}
    Teacher->>Planner: Ensure Placement (key=plan_id)
    Teacher->>Planner: Read durable planning-state
    Teacher->>Student: Read context / confirm path when needed
    Teacher-->>UI: Placement and planning state
    UI->>Teacher: Explicit Plan {diagnostic_plan_id}
    Teacher->>Planner: Same stable initial planning intent
    Teacher-->>UI: Durable planning state
```

## Ownership

`ms-go-teacher-agent` owns how the platform should teach a student:

- logical `PersonalTeacher` identity and preferences;
- teacher orchestration;
- bounded context construction;
- recognition and delegation of learning goals, requested skills, and replans;
- pedagogy, teaching, hint and intervention policies;
- explainable teacher decisions;
- immutable teacher-owned assistance summaries per learning action;
- LLM orchestration behind a port.

It does not own what the platform knows about a student. Mastery, evidence projection, learning paths, sessions, strengths, weaknesses and repeated mistakes belong to `ms-go-student`.

## Layers

```text
cmd/ms-go-teacher-agent/main.go
  -> internal/transport/http
  -> internal/transport/message/nats
  -> internal/infrastructure/persistence/postgres
  -> internal/infrastructure/messaging/nats
  -> internal/infrastructure/http/{student,course,dialog,aiprompt,learningplanner,statistic,telegram}
  -> internal/usecase
  -> internal/domain
```

- `internal/domain`: entities, value objects and outbound port interfaces.
- `internal/usecase`: application orchestration independent from HTTP, PostgreSQL, NATS and LLM SDKs.
- `internal/transport/http`: independent API, admin, private, and provider-signed integration contours.
- `internal/transport/message/nats`: strict durable inbound event decoding and acknowledgement.
- `internal/infrastructure`: PostgreSQL plus outbound service/messaging implementations.
- `cmd/ms-go-teacher-agent`: explicit composition root and lifecycle.

Architecture tests and `scripts/check_architecture.py` fail when dependencies point outward or unapproved directories appear.

As in `ms-go-course`, contour routers only register their own routes and explicit role policies. The root HTTP router composes trusted gateway-header authentication for API/admin and mounts the private and provider-signed contours independently. Concrete outbound HTTP clients are forbidden in transport and must use an approved `internal/infrastructure/http/<service>` path.

## Current foundation aggregate

`PersonalTeacher` is unique by `student_id`. It stores teacher profile and behavior configuration with optimistic `version`. Creating it is idempotent. It intentionally has no foreign key to another service database.

`TeacherSoul` is a separate one-to-one row bound by the same
`(personal_teacher_id, student_id)` pair. Every student therefore owns an
independently mutable logical teacher identity, voice, relationship style, and
encouragement style even when defaults initially match. Soul has its own
optimistic version and never becomes student memory: mastery, evidence, paths,
attempts, dialog history, raw events, prompts, and code are forbidden.

`TeacherDecision` stores an explainable business/pedagogical reason without chain-of-thought. It records the selected pedagogy method, method version, and method-neutral stage so replacements remain auditable. Task-scoped decisions carry the distinct `learning_action_id` as their correlation ID. Recording a decision and its schema-v2 `teacher.decision.recorded` event is one PostgreSQL transaction. A lease-based outbox relay uses `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`, bounded publish timeouts, exponential retry, JetStream acknowledgement, and `event_id` deduplication. Delivery remains at least once; consumers must maintain an inbox or processed-event ledger.

The service durably consumes `learning_action.closed` from `TASKANSWER_EVENTS`. The trigger carries a frozen target snapshot but no outcome. Finalization reads only teacher-owned decisions for that exact action cycle. No non-silent decision produces independent context; otherwise policy v1 records guided context, hint count/max level, and intervention, applying those action-level facts to every frozen target.

`LearningActionAssistance` stores that bounded summary over provider-neutral learning targets. The consumed inbox marker, assistance row, and `teacher.assistance.observed` outbox event commit in one transaction. A duplicate source `event_id` is a no-op. An action with zero targets commits only its inbox marker and emits no invented observations. The summary cannot carry objective outcome or mastery. `ms-go-student` consumes it through its own durable inbox.

`StudentContextBuilder` v1 is a synchronous bounded application capability. For a general dialog it loads Student's optional declared onboarding and at most 20 recent current mastery projections; self-assessment remains a hypothesis. For an action dialog it loads an ownership-scoped frozen action snapshot, requires the action to be open, and queries Student mastery only for the exact ordered targets in that snapshot. It returns an in-memory `StudentContext`; no student state is stored locally. Targetless actions remain empty, and Student dependency or contract failures fail closed. The closure finalizer remains independent and never calls Student synchronously.

The mounted Dialog boundary strictly decodes schema-v1
`dialog.teacher.requested` envelopes and persists a private `teacher_dialog_job`
before acknowledging. Duplicate event/source identities are accepted only when
all request metadata is identical. `general_teacher`, `lesson`, `lesson_task`,
`practice_task`, and `project` are claimed with a fenced lease by the
TeacherOrchestrator worker.

The student-facing provisioning use case derives `student_id` from the trusted
actor boundary, ensures that student's canonical PersonalTeacher, and calls
Dialog's internal idempotent ensure command. It validates the returned student,
teacher, context type, and context ID before exposing the Dialog-owned binding;
teacher-agent never creates or stores conversation rows itself.

For a claimed supported job, the worker verifies the PersonalTeacher and its exact
per-student soul, loads the
exact source plus at most 49 prior visible messages from Dialog, builds the
bounded Student context, and for action contexts reads only prior decisions for
that LearningAction.
`teacher-dialog-policy-v1` selects a registered deterministic `PedagogyMethod`
by `pedagogy_profile` before
model execution: Socratic question, direction, concept reminder, analogous
example, pseudocode, partial structure, then guided breakdown. The policy never
permits a complete solution. Its reason is a bounded business explanation,
never chain-of-thought. The registry has a safe default and no concrete-method
switch inside TeacherOrchestrator. A method exposes its own code/version and a
bounded generic stage, so future Bloom, ZPD, retrieval, or other implementations
can be added or replace an existing method at composition.

The model port calls AI Prompt's confidential `teacher.response.v1` contract
with exactly four variables: teacher profile (including the bound soul as
untrusted nested data), teaching plan, Student context,
and Dialog context. The source event ID is the generation and Dialog-append
idempotency key. A generation conflict is resolved through successful-result
replay. Teacher stores no prompt, variables, raw provider response, or context
snapshot.

Decision, `teacher.decision.recorded` outbox event, and the generated pending
body commit atomically. Delivery is a separate idempotent Dialog command. If the
process crashes after Dialog commits but before Teacher marks delivery, the
same append key returns the committed message. After validation, Teacher marks
the job delivered and clears the body. Dependency failures release the lease
with exponential retry; permanent identity/contract failures become blocked.
Response delivery does not wait for assistance consumption or mastery updates.

For `lesson`, each active source message carries a required `content_revision`
and non-empty `selected_text`. Teacher loads current active canonical text from
Course, requires the revision to match exactly, and verifies that the selected
text is an exact substring. Full Course text exists only as transient
verification input; the deterministic plan and AI Prompt receive only the
verified fragment. A changed revision, forged selection, inactive lesson,
deleted source, or malformed context fails closed. Course currently has no
immutable content-history or block identity, so the revision is the current
lesson `updated_at`; historical replay after an edit is intentionally refused.

`InterventionEngine` consumes bounded interesting-activity observations rather
than raw telemetry. A registry resolves `balanced`, `quiet`, or `proactive`
policy by the PersonalTeacher's `intervention_mode`; each implementation has a
stable code/version and can be replaced at composition. The default balanced
policy offers help only after at least three consecutive same-error failures
over at least 480 active seconds. Improving tests and idle time without stuck
evidence remain silent. Every signal produces a bounded business decision, and
an offer is delivered idempotently to the same general Dialog at most once per
analytics session. No LLM is invoked for this consent prompt.

Learning-session summary orchestration joins only two exact bounded
projections: an ended Student-owned session and its linked Statistic-owned
analytics summary. A deterministic versioned policy produces the localized
summary and next step. Teacher persists neither input. It delivers the result
to the same general Dialog with the Student learning-session UUID as an
idempotency key, then updates the Student-owned session counters with optimistic
concurrency. These are separate service calls; after a partial failure, retry
returns the same Dialog message and completes the Student projection.

For a course-linked ended session, the orchestrator submits a `REPLAN` intent
to Learning Planner after loading the current Student-owned learner overview.
The session result returns the planning request ID. Teacher neither reads a
Course curriculum projection nor computes or writes the next Student path.

The same delegation facade accepts an authenticated student's explicit desired
outcome, requested provider-neutral targets, and bounded constraints. It ensures
the student's PersonalTeacher and calls Learning Planner's dedicated Teacher
route with an idempotency key and optional Dialog/message/decision audit
references. Learning Planner owns graph traversal, mastery gap calculation,
course generation, assignment, and path replacement.

Learning Planner publishes terminal `course.plan.completed` and
`course.plan.failed` outcomes to `LEARNING_PLANNER_EVENTS`. Teacher's durable
consumer strictly validates the versioned envelope, ignores Student/System-owned
requests, and accepts each Teacher-owned event into a PostgreSQL inbox. When the
request includes an originating Dialog, it appends one bounded localized
business notification using the event ID as the Dialog idempotency key. It does
not expose provider errors, prompts, or hidden reasoning.

Default-dark product-aware onboarding uses a separate synchronous,
state-fenced Learning Planner readiness read. Teacher sends only the exact
Student state reference and accepts strict `learning-readiness.v1`; it never
sends a profile or graph. After an accepted Student effect, readiness resolves
before a deterministic response is staged. Recovery first proves the same S3
receipt. Teacher does not finalize Student state or invoke the S8 planning
mutation, and model text cannot make product claims.

Default-dark S8 transfers only an exact `READY` result into a Teacher-owned
durable handoff ledger before the S5 source lease is released. A separate
worker reuses one stable Planner command until strict `ACCEPTED`, checkpoints
that result, and then appends one deterministic plain Dialog message with a
second stable key. Source-bound delivery advances the dense cursor only in the
same transaction that completes the handoff, turn, job, and interaction. An
Ensure-origin handoff uses the same ledger without manufacturing a source job.
Planner acceptance is historical and non-executable (`NOT_STARTED`,
`NOT_CREATED`); executable planning and atomic current-state reservation are a
later owner boundary.

Next Best Action is a transient read of `ms-go-student` authority. Teacher reads
`student-next-action.v1` through the dedicated Student Teacher credential at
`GET /internal/students/{student_id}/next-action`, and forwards the exact primary,
secondary actions, reason, status, and provenance through its authenticated
next-action endpoint. Student owns precedence and the computed decision. Teacher
has no workspace traversal, fallback action selection, runtime state machine,
progress mutation, or LLM decision for NBA.

READY carries exactly one primary progression action. WAITING,
PLANNING_REQUIRED, and NO_PROGRESSION carry no executable primary. Optional
secondary actions remain separate from progression. Source context/path versions,
bounded runtime version, and state digest are preserved without local hashing.
A displayed decision is a snapshot, not a capability: owner commands revalidate
current invariants after explicit student intent.

Explicit English/Russian questions such as “What should I do now?” and
“Что мне делать сейчас?” in the general Dialog read Student NBA before prompt
construction and receive a deterministic explanation without AI Prompt. The
existing durable job, TeacherDecision/outbox, idempotent Dialog append, and retry
machinery deliver the explanation. Owner failure blocks/retries this request;
it never falls through to generation or creates a progression command.

Telegram is an optional transport around the same aggregate and Dialog
history. An authenticated student creates a short-lived one-time code; Teacher
stores only its SHA-256 digest and atomically binds a private Telegram user/chat
to that student's exact PersonalTeacher and general Dialog. Inbound plain text
uses Telegram `update_id` as deterministic Dialog idempotency evidence, so it
produces the ordinary `dialog.teacher.requested` pipeline. The source channel is
stored in the durable teacher job. After the canonical Dialog response commits,
Teacher idempotently creates one leased Telegram delivery row keyed by source
message ID. Telegram retry never rebuilds context or calls the model again.
Dialog remains the only conversation store.

The Bot API does not expose a caller idempotency key. The local queue therefore
guarantees one durable delivery intent and at-least-once attempts; an ambiguous
network acknowledgement can duplicate a Telegram transport message, but cannot
duplicate the Dialog message, teacher decision, or generation.

## Deferred boundaries

No direct Sandbox, raw Validation Orchestrator, or separate Knowledge Tree
integration is implemented. Practice and project dialogs read only the safe,
bounded current-task and optional validation-explanation projections from
Practice Runtime. Course task code reaches Teacher only through Student's
ownership-checked, bounded, secret-safe transient projection, which carries
only the latest mutation-invalidated validation/test pass flag, bounded issue
count, and time; raw test output is intentionally forbidden. Analytics
integration is asynchronous and bounded to interesting-activity observations;
raw events remain in Statistic. Course is used only for transient
lesson-selection verification; whole-lesson tutoring remains deferred until an
owner can prove student access and active position. The
closure and dialog pipelines do not resolve a graph: Course or the immutable
practice catalog revision supplies provider-neutral targets, Student freezes
them on the action, and Teacher uses those exact references. Learning Planner
is the sole planning-time owner of the target/prerequisite graph, so a second
Knowledge Tree service would duplicate ownership. Objective evidence projection
and mastery reduction remain owned by `ms-go-student`.

## Accepted Hybrid Replanning role (Problem #4)

Under the authoritative [Hybrid Mastery → Replanning decision](https://github.com/bemulima/ms-go-learning-planner/blob/main/docs/hybrid-mastery-replanning.md), Teacher may
request evaluation with an explicit reason and explain the resulting decision
from Evidence → Mastery Snapshot → Decision → Path Revision provenance. Student
coordinates the authoritative snapshot; Planner owns planning policy and
`NO_CHANGE` / `REPLAN_NEEDED`; Student validates and atomically applies at a safe
boundary. Teacher owns neither resulting Path computation nor direct Path writes
and cannot provide student consent for major changes.

This accepted target flow does not add a Teacher endpoint or alter existing
onboarding/diagnostic delegation. An evaluation request does not promise a Path
change. `OUT_OF_SCOPE_DEPENDENCY: NEXT_BEST_ACTION` is separate.
